caption: A handful of shredded cheese is scattered onto a hot skillet, and the shreds melt and flow together into a bubbling layer.

sa.check: Shredded cheese is scattered onto the skillet.
The shreds melt: they lose their strand shape.
The melted cheese flows together into one layer.
The layer bubbles at its edges.
The scattering comes first, then the melting, then the merging.

pc.expect: The shreds only soften, slump and join, and the layer's reach only grows; separate strands do not come back.
pc.fail: A melted patch separates into dry strands again; or the layer sets firm and matt in the hot pan; or the strands stiffen and stand up again; or the layer alternates between joined and separate.

pc.expect: Melting cheese slumps, goes glossy, stretches and pools as a thick liquid that bubbles, and the shreds soften before they join.
pc.fail: The shreds run as thin as water; or they shatter dry; or the layer stands as a rigid sheet that keeps its shape when the pan is tilted; or the shreds keep hard square edges while glossy and flowing.

pc.expect: The melted cheese runs into the pan's low places and spreads across its floor.
pc.fail: The cheese climbs the pan's wall and stays above the floor; or a run travels uphill; or melted cheese lifts off the pan and hangs.

pc.expect: The shreds melt where they touch the pan: they go glossy from underneath and the layer forms on the pan's floor.
pc.fail: Shreds high on a heap melt while those on the pan stay dry and separate; or a pool spreads on a part of the pan no cheese touched; or bubbles rise through the layer while the cheese is still dry strands.

pc.expect: The cheese in the layer is the cheese that was scattered, and it stays in the pan.
pc.fail: The layer grows with no cheese added; or shreds vanish with none joining the layer; or cheese appears outside the pan with none crossing the rim; or the pan changes shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The pan's surface and the hob around it stay the same.
pc.fail: The pan changes colour; or its handle changes shape; or items around the hob rearrange.

note: Browning of the cheese is chemistry and is not judged.
